_comment: Subquests by chapter: 125 recorded entries with the accept point, the location, the reward and the in-game deadline. Every entry carries a deadline in day/month form, which is what makes this list worth having: a subquest expires silently, and the reward is simply gone.

_mechanics.kinds: Two kinds are recorded. Generic subquests are taken from bulletin boards in Dagsion and appear on more than one route, while route-specific subquests belong to one lord~s path and can be missed entirely by choosing another.
_mechanics.priority: Priority subquests carry a real deadline. Missing one does not fail the run, it just deletes the reward, which for several of them is a class unlock rather than money.
_mechanics.dates: Deadlines are in-game dates in day/month form and are not tied to the real calendar. Several of them cluster on 27/11, which is the practical outer edge of Part I.
_mechanics.supplies: The Send Supplies chain on Theodora~s route all expires on 24/10, which is before Part I ends, so the items have to be collected early rather than banked.
_mechanics.semirandom: Four entries are recorded as likely semi-random generic subquests, because they do not appear in any published route walkthrough: Behelda Axes, Sinister Sacrifices, Energy Nuts and Soil Survey.
_mechanics.unlockQuests: Several subquests unlock classes outright, including Cataphract, Guardian, Dragoon, Dancer and Troubadour, which makes them the highest-value entries on the list.
_mechanics.paralogues: Paralogues are listed separately from subquests: they are unnumbered side chapters, not city errands, and the walkthrough page covers their route locks.

_openGaps: Missing NPC names: several entries record a location but no one to talk to, including Missing Master at Dagsion and Purloined Spellcaster~s Tools at the Secret Altar.
Deadline conflicts: the Dread Warrior Challenge series has two deadlines inside the same source, and three of those entries are grouped under a different chapter than the source states.
No year on the dates: deadlines are day/month only, so they are read as within-part dates rather than as a calendar.
No expiry confirmation for the entries listed as having no deadline, which means they are untested rather than safe.
